You are given an attached CSV file b3_fatigue_data.csv: 300 real samples,
the process/composition columns (NT, THT, THt, THQCr, CT, Ct, DT, Dt, QmT,
TT, Tt, TCr, C, Si, Mn, P, S, Ni, Cr, Cu, Mo, RedRatio, dA, dB, dC) and
column `target` (the measured rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa)).

Propose a recipe (a value for each variable below), within each observed
range, that MAXIMIZES rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa). Design
variables:
  - NT (value in [825, 930])
  - THT (value in [30, 865])
  - THt (value in [0, 30])
  - THQCr (value in [0, 24])
  - CT (value in [30, 930])
  - Ct (value in [0, 540])
  - DT (value in [30, 903.333])
  - Dt (value in [0, 70.2])
  - QmT (value in [30, 140])
  - TT (value in [30, 680])
  - Tt (value in [0, 120])
  - TCr (value in [0, 24])
  - C (value in [0.17, 0.63])
  - Si (value in [0.16, 2.05])
  - Mn (value in [0.37, 1.6])
  - P (value in [0.002, 0.031])
  - S (value in [0.003, 0.03])
  - Ni (value in [0.01, 2.78])
  - Cr (value in [0.01, 1.17])
  - Cu (value in [0.01, 0.26])
  - Mo (value in [0, 0.24])
  - RedRatio (value in [240, 5530])
  - dA (value in [0, 0.13])
  - dB (value in [0, 0.05])
  - dC (value in [0, 0.058])

Reason from the training data, then end with your explicit proposal, e.g.
"Final: NT=877.5, THT=447.5, THt=15, THQCr=12, CT=480, Ct=270, DT=466.666,
Dt=35.1, QmT=85, TT=355, Tt=60, TCr=12, C=0.4, Si=1.105, Mn=0.985, P=0.0165,
S=0.0165, Ni=1.395, Cr=0.59, Cu=0.135, Mo=0.12, RedRatio=2885, dA=0.065,
dB=0.025, dC=0.029".
turns.answer_text:
## Analysis of the training data

**Process route matters most.** The dataset contains three clear regimes:

1. **As-rolled / normalized only** (THT=30, no carburizing): targets ~225–275 MPa.
2. **Through-hardened + tempered** (THT≈825–865, TT=550–680): targets ~325–650 MPa. Within this group, lower tempering temperature (TT=550–580) and higher Ni/Cr/Mo help; a Si-rich, high-C subgroup (spring-steel-like) reaches 688–906 MPa.
3. **Carburized** (NT=930, THT=30/THt=0/THQCr=0, CT=930 with long carburizing time Ct, diffusion DT≈850–896, quench QmT, low-temperature temper TT=160, Tt=120, TCr=0.5): this group dominates, with targets 838–**1190 MPa**.

**Within the carburized group:**
- The best sample (1190 MPa) uses **Ct=540 (longest carburizing), DT=850, Dt=15, QmT=140, TT=160, Tt=120**.
- Comparing identical compositions: Ct=540/QmT=140 (1190) beats Ct=469.8/QmT=60 (1124); TT=160 generally ≥ TT=200.
- Best compositions in this group: **low C (~0.17–0.23), high Ni (~1.6–1.7), Cr ~0.45–0.6, Mo ~0.16–0.21, low P/S**. The Ni=1.69/Cr=0.55/Mo=0.18 alloy gives the two top results (1124, 1190).
- Low inclusion indices (dA, dB, dC) correlate weakly with higher strength within groups, so I trim dA slightly.

**Proposal:** essentially the empirically best carburized recipe — maximum carburizing time, diffusion at 850 °C, fast quench, low-temperature temper, Ni–Cr–Mo case-hardening chemistry with low C and clean steel (low P, S, inclusions).

Final: NT=930, THT=30, THt=0, THQCr=0, CT=930, Ct=540, DT=850, Dt=15, QmT=140, TT=160, Tt=120, TCr=0.5, C=0.23, Si=0.35, Mn=0.51, P=0.005, S=0.008, Ni=1.69, Cr=0.55, Cu=0.11, Mo=0.18, RedRatio=860, dA=0.02, dB=0.0, dC=0.0
